doc.title: Karl Berger interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, August 11, 2014

chapter: Free jazz, time and the Creative Music Studio
title: Meeting Ornette Coleman in 1965 and Eric Dolphy in 1964
summary: Berger recalls meeting Ornette in Paris in 1965 at the club where they played with Don Cherry, and knowing Eric Dolphy before his last Berlin gig in 1964.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: Well I’m going to guess that you probably had a different reaction to this LP than I did, the Free Jazz by Ornette Coleman. Did you know him when he did this?
No. No when was that? I think that was done in the late 50’s or early 60’s perhaps, 61 or something.
1960 yeah. So we met Ornette in ’65.
He came to Paris with his trio.
And then he came down to the club where we played with Don Cherry. That’s how we met Ornette. So that was ’65.
Okay. So I’m just going to put on —
Yeah we knew Eric the year before. We played with Eric on his last gig in Berlin and we actually brought him to the hospital. Yeah it was a sad situation. But that was ’64.
